Okay, so I'm trying to figure out why one puppy is much heavier than the others after six months. The options given are A) ate more food, B) was more active, C) drank more water, D) received more sunlight.

First, I remember that puppies, especially in a litter, are usually fed equally. So, the difference in size isn't likely due to the amount of food they ate. That makes me think option A is probably not the right answer.

Next, I think about activity. More active puppies tend to have better muscle development and stronger bones, which can make them appear heavier. They might also have a higher metabolism, burning more calories but also building more muscle. So, option B seems plausible.

Then, I consider water intake. While drinking more water is important for health, it doesn't directly affect weight gain. In fact, excessive water intake isn't typically linked to weight differences in puppies. So, option C doesn't seem right.

Lastly, sunlight exposure. Puppies don't get their nutrients from sunlight; they get it from their food. So, receiving more sunlight wouldn't make one puppy heavier. That rules out option D.

Putting it all together, the most likely explanation is that the more active puppy simply developed a different body composition, making it appear heavier.
